early.context: An affordable early 20-slot destination. Keep useful starting elites and substitute by role; do not delete them to match the list.
notes: Recruit towards this, not all at once

A developing army can remain below twenty until income supports it. When the hero is unavailable, replace that single slot with another shielded Spearman. A useful starting rocket, Ironside or rifle may replace one of the corresponding cheaper weapons.
Before the first Field Test is credited
Keep three ordinary Handgunners together with the named building requirement. Free Company Militia, Huntsmen and other unavailable or irrelevant units are not required.
Lower-cost escort
Use existing cavalry until you can afford the Empire Knights pair. When not working on the cavalry quest yet, another cheap infantry/ranged unit is a reasonable one-for-one stopgap.
plan: Hold a shape you can recognise

Deploy the line in several separated blocks, with clear gun lanes between or around them. Guns need line of sight; artillery and rifles do not shoot through your own infantry. Protect both ends rather than making an unbroken crowd.
One mobile reserve, one target at a time
Keep the mounted escort, or the machines in the late survey column, as a controlled reserve. Intercept a threat or punish an exposed flank; do not send each unit after a different distant target.
When the opening is over

Turn off pursuit where it is breaking your formation. Bring idle units to one useful segment. Keep a reserve behind the line and retreat a threatened gun section rather than letting it become an isolated melee unit.

notes: What is genuinely repeatable

Copy the generic commander version for ordinary armies when hero capacity allows it. Captain substitutes for Theodore only in Elspeth’s version; the generic roster has its own four-character package. Army-specific Elspeth skills and Garden travel do not transfer.
Affordable progression
Change one or two roles at a time and transfer displaced veterans to a relief army. Maintaining campaign momentum is better than sitting in Nuln for a perfect rebuild while targets expand.
Keep the escort relevant
The two Black Rose units are deliberate. Use them as one reserve or to clear an exposed rear; they are not meant to spend every battle charging braced spears.
An optional anti-large adjustment
Against repeated large-unit pressure, replace one Greatsword or anti-infantry battery with another Halberd/cannon-type answer as appropriate. Keep the total at twenty.

Elspeth’s optional eight-slot cap

After The Amethyst Armourer, extra one-for-one conversions are possible where the list has a compatible ordinary unit. Eight is an allowance, not a target. More generic armies do not increase it beyond the researched allowance.
Generic armies and scarce purchases

The generic character package can use this roster, but every army needs its own five purchased units. Keep most supporting armies on the ordinary Late or Mid template; do not hold the campaign hostage to purple stock.

legendary.role: This is a supporting army, not Elspeth’s main stack

home.context: Twelve slots by design. A garrison-backed response force, not a guarantee against an enemy full stack.
notes: Grow it only when the threat requires it
Add Halberdiers, a Priest and better gun support towards the Mid template when a real front develops. Do not recruit a decorative full stack that leaves the expedition unaffordable.
Keep an honest defence plan

Know which army can reinforce, whether the settlement can be bypassed, and whether the enemy brings two armies. Garden travel is helpful for Elspeth, but a cooldown prevents it being a permanent universal answer.
plan: Hold a shape you can recognise

Deploy the line in several separated blocks, with clear gun lanes between or around them. Guns need line of sight; artillery and rifles do not shoot through your own infantry. Protect both ends rather than making an unbroken crowd.
One mobile reserve, one target at a time
Keep the mounted escort, or the machines in the late survey column, as a controlled reserve. Intercept a threat or punish an exposed flank; do not send each unit after a different distant target.
When the opening is over

Turn off pursuit where it is breaking your formation. Bring idle units to one useful segment. Keep a reserve behind the line and retreat a threatened gun section rather than letting it become an isolated melee unit.
